01_nvidia-rtx-spark.json.title: Nvidia Just Built Its Own PC Chip — Intel and Qualcomm Are Rattled
01_nvidia-rtx-spark.json.script: For 30 years Nvidia has made the GPU. Never a full chip. Until now. At Computex, CEO Jensen Huang announced the RTX Spark — Nvidia's first processor in decades. It combines a Blackwell GPU with an Arm CPU, 128 gigabytes of unified memory, and runs Windows natively. Dell, ASUS, Lenovo, and Microsoft are all building laptops around it. Ships this fall. Intel and Qualcomm just lost their biggest moat.

04_nasa-space-chip.json.title: NASA's New Space Chip Is 500 Times More Powerful Than Any Before
04_nasa-space-chip.json.script: The computers guiding spacecraft today were designed in the 1990s. NASA just changed that. Its new High Performance Spaceflight Computing chip — built by Microchip Technology — is 500 times more powerful than current space computers, fits in your palm, and survives deep space radiation. It passed testing at JPL last month. Future rovers, lunar habitats, and deep space probes will run it. For the first time, spacecraft will be able to think for themselves.

05_brain-aging-nasal-spray.json.title: Scientists Reversed Brain Aging With a Nasal Spray. Alzheimer's Is Next.
05_brain-aging-nasal-spray.json.script: Texas A&M University just reversed brain aging — in mice — with a simple nasal spray. Researchers developed a spray using microscopic particles from neural stem cells. When given to 18-month-old mice — equivalent to 60-year-old humans — it reduced brain inflammation, restored memory, and produced benefits lasting months from just 2 doses. The team is now filing a patent. A human version is the next step. Alzheimer's may have met its match.

01_spacex-starship-catch.json.title: SpaceX Just Caught a Falling Skyscraper With Giant Chopsticks
01_spacex-starship-catch.json.script: For 60 years, every rocket launched was burned up or lost forever. SpaceX just broke that rule. On October 13, 2024, the Super Heavy booster — 70 meters tall, 33 engines — launched, completed its burn, and flew back to its launch tower. Giant mechanical arms called Mechazilla caught it mid-air. No splash landing. No parachutes. Just a skyscraper snapped out of the sky. Rocket reuse just became real.

America's most infamous nuclear site is now feeding artificial intelligence.

05_neuralink-first-patient.json.title: A Paralyzed Man Is Playing Chess By Thinking — Thanks to a Brain Chip
05_neuralink-first-patient.json.script: In January 2024, Noland Arbaugh became the first human to receive Neuralink's brain chip. He is paralyzed from the shoulders down. 8 weeks later, he was playing chess, browsing the web, and gaming — all by thinking. The N1 chip reads his brain signals, and a computer translates them to cursor movements. Zero physical movement required. Brain-computer interfaces just crossed from science fiction into everyday reality.
